1 Welcome to the monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners. We are happy to share information on significant news and events in Ada County. Ryan Davidson - Commissioner Rod Beck - Chairman Tom Dayley - Commissioner By the time you receive this month’s newsletter Election Day will be here! Everything you need to know about elections in Ada County can be found here: https://adacounty.id.gov/elections/ See for yourself why Ada County Elections is the gold standard in providing helpful voter information, transparency and security. Thank you to our Ada County Elections Director Saul Seyler and his staff for managing one of the most important functions of a vibrant democracy. ADA COUNTY ELECTIONS OFFICE BENJAMIN LANE RIBBON CUTTING October 2025 Thank you also to Ada County Operations project managers as well as Ada County Procurement for making sure another Ada County project is completed on time, on budget and in an efficient and frugal manner. Everything in this remodeled space is open, yet secure – all part of a concerted effort to make sure the public continues to have trust in our election system. Ada County’s secure elections system is considered the gold standard in this country. 3 No matter where you live in the United States, especially in rapidly growing Idaho, people are having a difficult time finding homes they can afford to buy. The Ada County Commissioners were proud to attend the groundbreaking ceremony in Boise on October 9, 2025, for the Dorado Station project. The housing development just off Fairview Avenue is made possible by a partnership between the City of Boise, J. Fisher Companies, Ada County, and the IHFA. Dorado Station will add 212 new affordable homes in Boise for residents who earn well below our area’s median income. The homes will be within walking distance of a major grocery store, a gym, a doctor’s office, and a bus route. Ada County provided $4.9 M of federal emergency rental assistance funding for this project. Rather than continue to pay monthly rents with that funding, the Board opted to do something more enduring, to benefit our Ada County community for years to come. “Everything the Board of Ada County Commissioners does is grounded in the concept of community benefit,” said Ada County Commission Board Chairman Rod Beck. “Every decision we make, every partnership we enter into, and every program we support revolves around what is best for our Ada County community.” DORADO STATION GROUNDBREAKING Pictured L-R: Boise City Council Member Jordan Morales, Boise City Council Member Jimmy Hallyburton, Ada County Commissioner Tom Dayley, Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck, Boise Mayor Lauren McLean, Boise City Council President Colin Nash, Boise City Council Member Meredith Stead, and Boise City Council Member Kathy Corless •Experts say no more than 28% of your gross monthly income (that’s pre-tax income) should go toward a mortgage. •The median household income in Boise is approximately $82,000.* (source: U.S. Census Bureau data) •The median home price in Ada County is approximately $555,000* (source: Boise Regional Realtors)

4 Community planners in Idaho must be experts on a wide variety of issues. A planner must have in-depth knowledge of complex land-use planning laws, zoning, property rights, transportation and housing, and effective public engagement. Planners must also understand how communities live, work, and play. Add to that – the delicate balancing act to accommodate growth and change. Ada County Development Services has a staff of dedicated planners who make this their goal every day. To honor this hard work and expertise, the Ada County Commissioners signed a proclamation designating October as Community Planning Month. The celebration allows us to publicly recognize the participation and dedication of county planners, planning commissions and other citizen planners who contribute their time and expertise to the constant improvement of Ada County. Thank you, Planners! CELEBRATING AND APPRECIATING COMMUNITY PLANNERS Pictured L-R: Ada County Commissioner Ryan Davidson, Ada County Development Services Director Richard Beck, Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck and Ada County Commissioner Tom Dayley. The short walk, in downtown Boise, starts at the Ada County Victim Services Center (ACVSC) and ends at the Ada County Courthouse on Front Street. We were honored to hear from Ada County Prosecutor Jan Bennetts, Ada County Sheriff Matt Clifford, Tamara Kelly, and Nursing Supervisor Anne Wardle. Do you know someone who may need help? The Ada County Victim Services Center in downtown Boise is a one-of-a-kind facility that provides comprehensive services in one location for those who experience interpersonal violence. 8 THE OWYHEE MOTORCYCLE CLUB A true County Treasure Congratulations to the Owyhee Motorcycle Club on being selected as this year’s Ada County Treasure for its historic association with recreation and culture in Ada County. If you haven’t heard about this club, it’s so worth knowing about. The Owyhee Motorcycle Club is the first motorcycle-related club or track in the country to be listed on the National Register of Historic Places. The private, member-supported club traces its history back to 1935 and was initially called the Western Ramblers Club. The Club was the first in the state of Idaho to charter with the American Motorcyclist Association (AMA) and is the oldest continuously operating club in the State of Idaho. The club has been at its current Boise Foothills location since 1946. The property and facility are significant for their role in the development of off-road motorcycle racing in Idaho and the Pacific Northwest. The Board of Ada County Commissioners and the Ada County Historic Preservation Council wish to acknowledge the efforts of the Owyhee Motorcycle Club for preserving this Ada County Treasure. Thank you to Ada County Commissioner Ryan Davidson for attending the recognition event. Ada County Commissioner Ryan Davidson and Owyhee Motorcycle Club President Megan McClurg at the October 19, 2025 event recognizing the club’s historical significance Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck and Owyhee Motorcycle Club President Megan McClurg

9 WHAT ARE COUNTY TREASURES? Every year The Ada County Historic Preservation Council recognizes sites or structures that add to and preserve Ada County’s Heritage and are maintained through the dedication of caring individuals, groups and businesses. If you would like to nominate a site or structure, please contact bdanielson@adacounty.id.gov WHAT ARE THE CRITERIA FOR BEING A COUNTY TREASURE? ● Structure(s) must be at least 50 years old. ● Must be located in Ada County, with a preference in unincorporated Ada County, or must be related to the County’s rural history, government history or early infrastructure. ● Must have historic significance (properties which are listed on the National Register of Historic Places or a city/Ada County historic resource inventories will also qualify). ● The property/structure should exhibit uniqueness and must still be serviceable or in reasonably well-preserved condition. 11 SHERRY MORGAN – 30 YEARS OF SERVICE TO ADA COUNTY On behalf of Ada County and the Ada County Prosecutor’s Office, we want to express our deepest gratitude to Sherry Morgan for 30 years of exceptional service. Sherry’s sharp legal mind, consistently high-quality work, and clear, timely communication have been invaluable to the elected offices and departments she serves and to our entire team. Sherry approaches every matter with professionalism, sound judgment, and a collaborative spirit that makes her a trusted partner across the county. Pictured L-R: Ammon Taylor, Prosecutor’s Office; Robert Berry, Prosecutor’s Office; Logan Weis-Hurzeler, Prosecutor’s Office; Tom Dayley, Ada County Commissioner; Jan Bennetts, Ada County Prosecutor; Shery Morgan, Prosecutor’s Office; Rod Beck, Ada County Commission Chairman; Heather McCarthy, Prosecutor’s Office; Ryan Davidson, Ada County Commissioner Sherry’s ability to work seamlessly with county departments, distill complex issues, and deliver dependable legal guidance has strengthened both our operations and our public service. Colleagues rely on her expertise and integrity, and her steady presence has made a lasting difference in the Civil Division and to Ada County as a whole. Thank you for three decades of unwavering dedication, excellence, and commitment to Ada County. We celebrate this milestone with sincere appreciation and look forward to continuing to work with you. ADA COUNTY GOVERNMENT In addition to elected offices, Ada County government includes twelve individual departments. Each department provides important services to our residents in Star, Eagle, Meridian, Boise, Garden City, Kuna, and Unincorporated Ada County. These services include law enforcement protection, emergency preparedness, election services, parks & waterways, indigent services, juvenile services, solid waste management, the Western Idaho Fair, Weed, Pest & Mosquito Abatement and more. Learn more about the services provided to you by Ada County - www.adacounty.id.gov/

13 DO YOU KNOW WHERE KEY ADA COUNTY CITIES AND LANDMARKS ARE? If you’re new to the area or if your family has lived in Idaho for generations, it’s critically important to know at least a little bit about the layout of your community. Where is your town in relation to other cities? What city in Ada County is actually in two different counties? Where is Lucky Peak Dam? Where is Expo Idaho? Good questions! We have updated our Ada County illustrated map with some new key landmarks noted. We’ve also updated our city population* numbers. You’ll notice that Unincorporated Ada County (the area of the county that is not within a city’s jurisdiction) has a population larger than some cities. *Population estimates are estimates of the current population in a particular area. Each year, COMPASS develops population estimates for city and county jurisdictions in Ada and Canyon Counties.

Director Schroeder is working to build a coalition to ask the legislature for financial support to address the growing rat problem.
